persons.name: [?] G. Abbot
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Abbot, 8. G.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. AN INITIAL THIS PROJECT CANNOT READ, MARKED AS ONE. The card shows '[?] G. Abbot': the scan sets a DIGIT where the middle initial goes, and a digit is never part of a name, so the character is carried as [?] — the marker the Chicago list of 1 January 1834 already uses for an initial the printing did not deliver. NO LETTER IS SUPPLIED. The deposit holds two transcriptions of this issue and no page image, and the alternate carries no letter list at all, so there is no cleaner impression here to settle it against and the project declines to guess (T-0721; the suspicion is registered, ungraded, at data/research/residents/letter_list_reading_suspicions.json). The verbatim setting is untouched and quoted above; what has stopped is the card asserting that setting is a name. A pass that reaches the page images settles it and this marker goes. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. persons.name: A O T Bread
persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST ALONE. Read from poll_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1835 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of 1835 — “Bread, A.O.T.” (poll_1835_009, line 294). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Bread' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

persons.name: Henry S Handy
persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from death_notice, newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 18 March 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “HANDY HENRY S”, 1835-06-27 to 1835-09-10: 2 federal land entries — SE sec 14 T38N R14E; W2SW sec 22 T38N R14E, 240.00 acres stated in all, for $300.00 (ls0611, ls0636). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: HANDY HENRY S matches Henry S Handy: the forename names Henry S Handy of the 2 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

persons.name: Kai Bai Squam
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1376, stage `underdocumented`). Enrolled at Chicago in 1832 in the company the Black Hawk War roll heads INDIAN, with no 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — the same roll, the same year, the same page — and the twenty men of Kercheval's company the town already carries were re-admitted under it. The roll prints him as `KAI BAI SQUAM`, company `INDIAN`, enrolled at `CHICAGO`. The research READ this name and WITHHELD it, and that refusal is not overturned: this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence, and it says so on its face. The reading, the source and the refusal stand at `civic:data/research/civic/records/blackhawk_war_1832_chicago.json#records/blackhawk_1832_037#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native person at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.

District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.

what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.
